summary.en-US: Marks posts and comments on Reddit, LinkedIn, Hacker News and X as AI-written or human. The model runs in your browser, so no text leaves your computer.

description.en-US:
Slop Detect puts a badge next to posts and comments on Reddit, LinkedIn, Hacker News and X: "AI 0.93" or "Human 0.04", the model's estimate of whether a text was written by AI.

- It runs locally: the model runs in your browser, and no text leaves your computer.
- On first use it downloads the model from Hugging Face, once: 450 MB.
- On the CPU it is slow. With WebGPU it runs on the graphics card; on Linux, switch WebGPU on first by setting `dom.webgpu.enabled` to `true` in `about:config`.
- It scores English texts, and the score is an estimate that can be wrong.
- Alt+Shift+D switches it on or off.

This is a Firefox port of Slop Detect by Voight-Kampff Labs: https://github.com/voightkampfflabs/slop-detect-extension

version.approval_notes:
The extension is built with WXT and Vite from the attached sources, on Linux with Node 24 and npm 11 (built here with Node 24.20.0 and npm 11.19.0):

npm ci
npm run build -- -b firefox

The extension is then in .output/firefox-mv2, identical to the submitted file. README.md has the same steps.

The ort-wasm-simd-threaded*.mjs and .wasm files are onnxruntime-web 1.31.1 files from npm, unchanged but for their names. ort.webgpu.bundle.min-*.js and ort.wasm.bundle.min-*.js are its dist/ort.webgpu.bundle.min.mjs and dist/ort.wasm.bundle.min.mjs, re-bundled by Vite. The model is downloaded from huggingface.co only after the user clicks "Download model".
